facts.text: The Tamsui River Mangrove Nature Reserve lies along the Tamsui River near Zhuwei; the Mangrove Ecocenter is reached from Exit 2 of MRT Hongshulin Station.
The area was declared a nature reserve in 1986 and covers about 76 hectares.
Ordinary tourists may not enter the reserve itself; a wooden boardwalk runs along its edge for visitors.
The main tree of the reserve is Kandelia, called water pen in Chinese, and the reserve protects this forest and the animals living in it.
Kandelia seeds start to sprout while still on the parent tree; the long, pen-shaped seedlings hang from the branches, then drop into the water or mud and take root.
Mangrove trees can live in very salty water, and they have shallow, wide-spreading roots, including roots that help support the trees.
At high tide most of the marsh is under water and only the tops of the mangrove trees show; at low tide wide mudflats appear.
The mudflats are home to fiddler crabs and mudskippers, and egrets and other water birds come to feed there.
Migratory birds such as teals and herons visit the area every winter.
Mudskippers are fish that spend much of their time out of the water on mudflats.
